vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: video-generator-auto-post
Version: 1.1.0

The skill is classified as suspicious because it explicitly sets up the framework for handling sensitive API keys and performing network operations to external social media platforms, even though the core posting functionality in `scripts/auto-post.py` is currently a stub (marked with `TODO`s). The `SKILL.md` instructs users to configure API keys in a `.env` file, which `scripts/auto-post.py` loads. While there is no evidence of immediate malicious intent, data exfiltration, or active vulnerabilities in the provided code, the clear intent and preparation for risky capabilities (handling credentials, external network communication) without full implementation makes it not entirely benign, as future completion could introduce vulnerabilities.

llm.summary: This skill is not malicious, but it needs Review because it asks for social-account posting credentials and automated public posting without enough safeguards or accurate implementation disclosure.

dimensions.detail: Local GPU video-generation setup is proportionate to the purpose, but asking users to configure social API keys for automated posting is high-impact and under-scoped.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Setup is user-directed and visible, but it instructs users to install unpinned Python packages and imports python-dotenv without documenting that dependency.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill includes broad trigger phrases and a default all-platform posting command, but does not require a confirmation, dry run, platform-by-platform review, or clear warning before public account actions.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No persistence, privilege escalation, background worker, or destructive local behavior was found; the main sensitive element is credential use through a local .env file.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is AI video generation plus automatic social publishing, but the artifact only includes a prompt guide and an auto-post script whose platform upload methods are TODO stubs; several referenced generation, batch, optimization, reference, and asset files are absent.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review this carefully before installing. Do not put real social-media API keys in .env or run posting commands until the publisher adds clear confirmation, dry-run behavior, least-privilege setup instructions, pinned dependencies, and accurate documentation of what is actually implemented.
llm.findings:
[TP4] unexpected: Artifact inspection supports a capability mismatch: the documentation advertises generation and auto-posting, while included executable code is only a posting scaffold and does not actually upload.
[LP3] unexpected: No explicit tool scope is declared, which matters because the skill discusses package installation, local model setup, API keys, and public posting.
[SQP-2] expected: Social posting is purpose-aligned, but the artifact lacks clear warnings, least-privilege guidance, confirmation, or dry-run controls for public platform actions.
[SQP-1] unexpected: The broad generation trigger could invoke the skill for ordinary video requests even though the skill also contains automated posting workflows.
[SDI-1] unexpected: The included platform methods return success after printing status and contain TODO comments for the real API uploads, so the advertised auto-publish feature is not implemented.
[T08] unexpected: The unpinned pip install instruction is a real supply-chain hygiene issue, though no malicious dependency or hidden install behavior was found in the artifact.
[SQP-3] expected: The Chinese branding text appears disclosed as author branding and is not security-significant by itself.
